name: Bartholomew
overview: Bartholomew was a male disciple of the Messiah and one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus, as recorded in Matthew 10:2-3. While his surname Bartholomew means 'son of Tolemay,' some scholars view this as a patronymic rather than a proper name. He is also identified with Nathanael in John 1:45, suggesting a dual naming in the New Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Bartholomew means 'son of Tolemay,' indicating a familial lineage, while Nathanael means 'G-d has given,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning. Both names are proper names given by people rather than directly by God, as noted in the biblical references Matthew 10:3 and John 1:45.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Bartholomew as a disciple and apostle of YHVH, the Messiah, according to Matthew 10:3. Beyond his role as a follower of Christ, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Bartholomew holds significance as one of the Twelve Apostles personally chosen by Jesus to be His closest followers and messengers. His identification with Nathanael in John’s Gospel adds depth to his biblical identity, linking him to a figure recognized for sincere faith. His role as an apostle underscores his participation in the foundational ministry of Christ and the early church.
